poc_plan: Objective: validate Dedicated capacity for realtime telemetry alerting under production-like load
Duration: 2 weeks (1 week load tests + 1 week soak/stability + final verification)
Environment: Dedicated cluster — initially 4x A100-80GB (reserved), autoscale policy to +2 nodes for bursts
Workloads: mixed-query mix — 60% short chat-style alerts (<=64 tokens), 30% embeddings (512 tokens), 10% multi-turn generation (~512-1024 tokens)
Throughput targets: sustained 300 qps for short alerts, peak bursts to 750 qps for 5 min windows
Latency SLOs: target p95 <= 80ms for short alert responses; p99 <= 200ms for short; generation p95 <= 450ms
Soak tests: 48h continuous at 85% sustained throughput to validate memory leak/KV cache behavior
Load tests: step ramp from 10 qps -> 750 qps over 45 mins, repeated 4x with model routing changes
Representative prompts: provided sample set (sensors anomaly texts, root-cause summarization, similarity queries) — will drive token distribution
Model strategy: primary: optimized open-model-medium (quantized); fallback: smaller quantized variant for burst shedding
Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 per route, tokens/sec/node, GPU util, tail latency events, failed requests %, cold-start distribution
Success criteria: meet latency SLOs <= 95% of time during sustained window + linear cost projection under reserved pricing
Deliverables: perf report, cost projection, GPU sizing recommendation, SLA draft with uptime/throughput guarantees
notes: AE notes: Ashwood very sensitive to tail latency — 'if the alert is late it's useless'
SE notes: prefer VPC peering for lower network variance; KMS integration timeline could add 2 weeks
Commercial: negotiating committed qps vs committed token volume. They want a hard throughput guarantee for peak 5-min windows.
Security: audit logs retention request = 5 years for certain telemetry types; legal asked about encryption in transit+at rest
Technical risk: embedding cold-cache fill caused 30% higher latency in early run; planning to pre-warm KV cache and prefix caching
Routing: will test policy: latency-priority -> cost-priority fallbacks; measure regression on quality when falling back to quantized model
Cost sensitivity: mid-high; willing to commit if unit economics under reserved plan show >=30% saving vs on-demand cloud GPUs
Quote from CTO (2026-02-28): 'We need guarantees for both throughput and predictable unit cost — can't accept opaque burst billing.'
Next internal: SE to supply detailed test harness (k6 + custom token generator) and a redline SLA for Ashwood legal
